samples.evidence: The test sets focus `{offset: 5, lineAffinity: 'forward'}` with anchor at offset 10 and asserts one rect at LINE1_Y. But buildRects now defaults an affinity-less start to `'forward'` (`const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'`, selection.ts), so the very same rects are produced if getNormalizedRange dropped the endpoint object (and its lineAffinity) entirely. verdict.reason: Verified directly. The reversed-range test (selection-line-affinity.test.ts:127-136) passes focus {offset:5, lineAffinity:'forward'} and asserts exactly one rect at LINE1_Y — the identical assertions used by the affinity-less default test at lines 117-125. Because buildRects defaults an absent start affinity to 'forward' (src/view/selection.ts:260), stripping lineAffinity during normalizeRange's swap (src/view/selection.ts:174-180) produces byte-identical rects, so the test cannot fail on the behavior its own comment claims to cover ("its affinity must survive"). The contrasting 'backward' start does yield a different, detectable shape (>1 rect, first at LINE0_Y — lines 104-115, driven by pagination.ts:401-407), confirming the discriminating variant the reviewer proposes. The only thing this test can detect is endpoint ordering (unswapped -> blockStart >= blockEnd -> continue -> zero rects, selection.ts:463-467), not affinity propagation. No other test covers it: only selection-line-affinity.test.ts and hf-caret-selection.test.ts mention lineAffinity, and the latter concerns header/footer caret placement. Real, in-lane (non-discriminating test presented as coverage for a behavior change), and major under the rubric.

verdict.reason: The four claimed producers are real and present: text-editor.ts:1517-1525 (mousedown DocPosition gets lineAffinity), 1776/1798 (drag focus endpoints, body and header/footer), 2772-2780 (shift+arrow focus gets focusAffinity), 2806-2814 (shift+Home focus hard-codes 'forward'). Searching /affinity/i across every test root in all packages yields only three files: selection-line-affinity.test.ts (direct computeSelectionRects call with hand-built endpoints), hf-caret-selection.test.ts (direct computeHFCursorPixel/computeHFSelectionRects calls, no TextEditor), and frontend yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts:441-472 (store anchor round-trip for the caret, not a text-editor endpoint producer). No docs test synthesizes a mouse hit (clientX|mousedown|clickAt across packages/docs/test yields only editor-contextmenu.test.ts:72, a contextmenu event), so the mousedown/drag producers are unreached directly or indirectly. Shift-key tests that drive the real editor assert offsets only (editor-read-only.test.ts:341-362 checks focus.offset===1); no test does a strict toEqual/deepEqual on a selection range, and no test captures selection rects from a live editor, so there is no implicit geometric assertion either. Every one of these endpoint-affinity producers could revert to {blockId, offset} and the suite would stay green — a clear behavior change with no meaningful test, major under the test-adequacy rubric.

I chased the indirect routes: hf-caret-selection.test.ts does populate blockParentMap with a cell (:154-156) and does test affinity, but it exercises computeHFSelectionRects, a separate implementation in editor.ts:798 delegating to computeHFTableCellSelectionRects, which never enters buildRects — and its cell case (:168-181) passes endpoints without lineAffinity anyway. peer-cursor.test.ts calls resolvePositionPixel only with 'backward' and an empty blockParentMap (:84-132). cell-range-expand.test.ts:141 constructs Selection but never asks for rects. In-lane for test-adequacy (changed behavior with no meaningful test), major impact.

verdict.reason: The store change is real: anchorDocRange forwards per-endpoint affinity (yorkie-doc-store.ts:994-1005) into anchorDocPosition (:918,:939) and resolveAnchoredDocPosition spreads it back (:1059,:1077,:1129), reached for selections via resolveAnchoredLocalCursor (:1173-1174) and updateCursorPos (:3001). A repo-wide grep for `lineAffinity` finds only three test files: the frontend integration file plus two packages/docs view tests. The docs tests are view-level rect math (selection-line-affinity.test.ts:1-6 imports computeSelectionRects with a stub measurer) and never touch YorkieDocStore. In frontend, only the single-caret test (integration.ts:441-472) uses affinity, and it goes through anchorDocPosition via updateCursorPos(pos), not anchorDocRange. The two selection-endpoint tests (:474-499, :501-529) pass endpoints without affinity and assert shapes without it; they would catch injection of a constant affinity but cannot fail if the per-endpoint forwarding is removed, so the new positive behavior (a 'forward'/'backward' endpoint affinity surviving anchor -> upstream edit -> resolve, incl. reversed anchor/focus) has no test. Missing coverage for a real behavior change: major and in-lane.

finding.summary: None of the text-editor plumbing that actually produces the affinity is tested (click, shift+click, drag, shift+Home, shift+arrow)
finding.evidence: The user-visible fix is that a click/drag/caret-move on a wrap boundary tags the selection endpoint with `lineAffinity` (text-editor.ts ~1517 mousedown, ~1770 header/footer drag, ~1792 body drag, ~2772 shift+arrow, ~2805 shift+Home). The only new test, packages/docs/test/view/selection-line-affinity.test.ts, hand-constructs DocPositions and calls `computeSelectionRects` directly — it never goes through TextEditor, so it cannot fail if the editor forgets to attach the affinity, attaches the wrong one (e.g. the shift+Home hardcoded 'forward' at offset 0, or shift+Up/Down using the cursor's stale affinity), or drops it on `setRange`. I grepped packages/docs/test for `lineAffinity` (only the new file and hf-caret-selection.test.ts, which tests computeHFCursorPixel), and for `Home|getVisualLineStart|updateDragSelection|mousedown|mousemove` (only cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts and image-selection-overlay.test.ts, neither of which touches selection affinity). Result: the entire producer side ships with zero coverage while the rect consumer is well covered.

verdict.reason: The affinity producers in text-editor.ts are real and untested. Verified code sites: mousedown attaches lineAffinity (text-editor.ts:1517-1525), drag selection attaches it on the header/footer (1776) and body (1798) branches, shift+arrow sets focus.lineAffinity (2772-2780), and handleHome hardcodes 'forward' (2803-2818). The only new test, packages/docs/test/view/selection-line-affinity.test.ts, imports computeSelectionRects directly (line 2), builds fake layouts, and feeds literal endpoint objects via rectsFor (lines 80-89); it never constructs a TextEditor, never calls Selection.setRange, and dispatches no events, so it cannot fail if the editor omits or mis-sets the affinity. I searched repo-wide for `lineAffinity` and for `affinity` in all packages/**/*test* files: the only other hits are hf-caret-selection.test.ts (pure computeHFCursorPixel/computeHFSelectionRects, describes at :52/:109) and packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts:441-468, which covers the caret anchor round-trip in the Yorkie store, not editor selection plumbing. No packages/docs test dispatches mousedown/mousemove (only editor-contextmenu.test.ts:68 contextmenu and image-selection-overlay.test.ts image logic); 'Home' appears only in a comment (cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts:11), whose pressArrow (:115-136) dispatches unshifted arrows and asserts measureText counts; keyboard editor tests (backward-selection-toggle.test.ts) set ranges via _setSelectionForTest and assert inline styles only. No co-located src tests and no e2e dir. The jsdom editor harness plus _getCursorForTest (editor.ts:360-364) shows such tests are feasible, so this is a genuine gap on the user-visible behavior, i.e. major under the missing-tests rubric.
